title: Build Claude Code reply fixtures with MakeMe steps

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: one targeted break check

Verdict: Caught. Next proof action: none needed for this path. The maintained assertion caught the fault.

Story and revision: .planning/seeds/SEED-422-correct-stale-dashboard-token-totals.md#build-claude-reply-fixtures-with-makeme ("Build Claude Code reply fixtures with MakeMe steps"), plan .planning/slice-plans/773-build-claude-reply-fixtures-with-makeme/PLAN.md. Revision f2de57e1722eef2865ee01249c9aa8dc576af61e, run in a scratch detached worktree at /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/2923cefa/tmp/ic-checkout (npm ci, node v24.21.0). The worktree had no changes before the probe and has since been removed. The execution checkout was not touched and stash was not used.

Promise: the rewritten ClaudeTranscriptBuilder steps still feed the scenario the Usage spec assertions protect. In particular, `withDeveloperReply` must still supply the reply's 300-output-token response, so the developer-reply launch index stays at 6,850 (launch 1,950 + reply 2,950 + worker 1,950).

Fault (I used the suggested one unchanged): in Distribution/tests/support/claudeTranscriptTestData.mjs, `withDeveloperReply()` now sends the `after-reply` response with `outputTokens: 200` instead of 300. That was the only edit, and I left the fixtures and assertions alone.

Focused command (checkout root): caffeinate -s -i env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES OPEN_DOUGH_DASHBOARD_BACKEND_PROOF_RECORD=<path>.json npm run --silent test:dashboard:backend -- dashboard/backend-tests/usage-history/token-index-developer-reply.spec.ts

Runs (from the proof records):
- Baseline: phase completed, selectedCount 5, all 5 passed, strictStatus passed. The 5 tests cover the reply plus worker case, the reply after the completion report, two workflow-typed/slash landing variants and the second launch's reporting context.
- Faulted: 4 of 5 failed and strictStatus failed. The first failure is at token-index-developer-reply.spec.ts:54 `expect(index).toEqual([["SEED-7#claude", 6_850]])`, which expected 6850 and received 6350. Two more failures are at :112 (the workflow typed and slash workflow variants), where the `outputs(... task.workflow)` toEqual expected "execution": 400 and received 300. The last is at :139 (the second launch), where the launchReference outputs expected 400 for the first launch and received 300. The "reply after completion report" case (4,900) still passed, which is expected because it writes its reply rows inline and does not call `withDeveloperReply`.
- Reach and wrong behavior: I checked these independently against the fixture arithmetic. Each output token weighs 5 index units, so 100 fewer reply output tokens should lower the index by exactly 500 (6,850 to 6,350), and the execution task's stored output tokens should fall from 400 to 300 (100 launch + 200 reply). The received values match these numbers exactly. So the faulted builder step reached the importer and index on the intended path, and the product reported the wrong totals that the assertions protect.
- Restored: the fault was undone with git checkout through an EXIT trap. git status showed 0 changes and HEAD was still f2de57e17. Rerunning the same command passed 5 of 5 with strictStatus passed.

Scope limits: I only probed token-index-developer-reply.spec.ts. I did not run token-index-refresh-developer-reply.spec.ts or token-index-provisional.spec.ts against this fault. I did not separately probe the 1,950 / 10,900 values, coverage kinds or medians, or the `withCountedOpusResponse` and `withWorkerResult` steps. No repair was already planned for this path, and the probe raises no new repair decision.

Cost:
- Test runtime (measured, Playwright runner durationMs from the proof records): baseline 23.4 s, faulted 20.1 s, restored 14.8 s, about 58.3 s in total. Wall-clock times including the npm wrapper were 29 s, 24 s and 17 s.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part in the run and there is no separate measure.
- Agent effort: unavailable. There is no separately supported token or time measure for this agent. The elapsed time below is the only measured proxy.
- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 154248 ms (measured), from 1795342235000 to 1795342389248 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: checked f2de57e1722eef2865ee01249c9aa8dc576af61e; Caught; no follow-up.
